en: The Sutra of the Twenty-One Homages to the Mother Who Saves from Peril.
*Namo āryāvalokiteśvarāya mahākāruṇikāya*.
Homage to the Noble Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, the Treasury of Great Compassion.
In the sublime realm of Potala, she arises from the green syllable DAṂ;
she is the Mother of the activities of the Buddhas of the three times.
Adorned on her crown by Amitābha, she is further graced by the crests of all devas and asuras. With reverent prostration, they kneel and offer their lotus hands at her two feet.
The Mother who delivers all from poverty and suffering; Before the Buddha-mother Tārā, I pay homage:
Oṃ, homage to the Noble and Holy Tārā.
Oṃ, homage to Tārā, the swift and heroic; Tāre, tāre, you who remove fear!
I praise and pay homage to the one who bestows all ultimate meanings,
the syllable Svāhā, the swift and heroic Mother of Deliverance; whose eyes flash like lightning for a moment,
illuminating the three worlds, the Honored One with a lotus face, appearing in exquisite beauty from within a wondrous flower.

Homage to the Mother who is like the autumn moon of a hundred autumns, Whose stainless face shines universally and perfectly, Gathering together like a thousand constellations; Her sublime majesty surpasses them all.
Homage to the Mother of purple-gold hue, Whose hand is exquisitely adorned with a wondrous lotus.

Homage to the Tathāgata Uṣṇīṣavijayā, who practices generosity, diligence, gentleness, and tranquility; who possesses patience and meditative concentration, whose nature is free from objective realms, and who is revered by all.
She is the most supreme, capable of fulfilling boundless conduct and virtues, having reached the further shore without exception;
she is the mighty one, most dearly beloved by the sons of the Buddha.
Homage to the Mother of the syllables Tā-ra-hūṃ! With the sound of her love, she fills the directions and the entirety of space;
With her striding feet, she traverses the seven worlds, Able to summon and gather all without exception.
Homage to the Mother of Śakra, Brahmā, and Agni, To whom the wind-gods and the hosts of Īśvara have gathered!
The bhūtas, vetālas, gandharvas, and the hosts of yakṣas all offer praise and prostrate to Tārā, Mother of the World.
She utterly destroys the ritual applications of others;
she stands with her left leg extended and her right drawn in, treading upon [the foe]. Her topknot is blazing and intensely radiant.
Homage to Tārā, the Great Vidyārājñī, The courageous one who can crush the hosts of māras and enemies;
Who frowns upon her lotus-like face, And destroys all multitudes of adversaries.
Homage to the Mother adorned with the seals of the Triple Gem, Whose hand is placed at her heart in a majestic posture.
Homage to the Mother of Majestic Power and Joy, who adorns the square wheel in its entirety without exception;
she whose own body is a mass of blazing light, adorned with jewel-light and pearl garlands,
laughing most exceedingly, and who subdues the māras of the world.
Homage to the Mother who protects all the stages,
Who can summon the hosts of deities with a frowning brow and the syllable HŪṂ, Who delivers all from ruin and decay;
Homage to the Mother whose crown bears the form of the moon, In whose crown appears the most excellent and wondrous radiance.
Manifesting from within the topknot of Amitābha Buddha, Constantly emitting the radiance of myriad wondrous jewels;
I pay homage to her who dwells like the extinguishing of the kalpa-fire, Abiding within the blazing uṣṇīṣa,
seated in the universal joy of the half-lotus posture, Able to crush and destroy the wheel of evil enemies.
Homage to the Mother who presses the earth with her hand, Who treads upon it with her feet to suppress it,
Whose brow is knit and who utters the sound "Hūṃ," Able to shatter the seven calamities and subdue all;
Homage to the Mother of peace, gentleness, and goodness, The realm of supreme bliss, the tranquility of *nirvāṇa*.
Homage to the Mother of Universal Great Joy, who is endowed with the seed-syllable *svāhā*, who is well able to eliminate great calamities,
who causes all enemies to be severed from their limbs,
whose ten-syllable mantra is exquisitely arrayed, and whose sound of the vidyā-mantra *hūṃ* is ever radiant.
Homage to the Mother Duritāntakṛt! With her feet she treads upon the *mṛga* and *manduka*, And from the seed-syllable *Hūṃ*, she causes these three places to tremble.
Homage to the Mother Sarasvatī, the ocean of gods, Who holds in her hand the image of the divine beast (*śarabha*).
Reciting the two *tāras* produces a resonant sound that can utterly extinguish all poisons without remainder.
Homage to the Mother of the Assembly of Devas, the beloved refuge of the gods and *kiṃnaras*, whose majesty brings joy like firm armor; she eliminates strife and evil dreams.
Homage to the Mother of Vast Circular Sun and Moon, Whose gaze surpasses the light of universal radiance;
Reciting twice *hara-dut-tarī*, she skillfully removes Malignant poisons and fevers of pestilence.
Homage to the Mother Endowed with the Three Realities, Who possesses the power of perfect tranquility.
Yakṣas seize and possess beings, yet Tārā most effectively removes all calamities and misfortunes.
If there is one who is wise and exerts diligent effort,
reciting this with a sincere heart and prostrating with true faith before the Honored One who Saves through Twenty-one Names— therefore, praise the Root Mantra.
Rising early every morning and performing worship at evening, Recalling and bestowing supreme fearlessness upon all,
All karmic offenses will be completely eliminated, And one will be able to transcend all evil realms.
Such as these shall swiftly attain wisdom, Having been consecrated by seventy million Buddhas.
May there be prosperity, nobility, and long life in this present world, and may one proceed toward the rank of all Buddhas in the future.
Should one ever mistakenly consume various poisons— whether naturally occurring or synthetically compounded—
by recollecting the true power of the Noble Honored One, all evil poisons shall be utterly extinguished.

If one sees others beset by malevolent spirits, or afflicted with fevers and various sufferings, by reciting this praise two, three, or seven times, all those pains and afflictions will be entirely dispelled.
Those who wish to beg for children shall obtain children; those who seek wealth, treasures, or rank shall attain abundance.
To the Noble Mother, the Honored Tārā, who skillfully fulfills all wishes as desired and whom no obstacles can assail;
and to all the Buddhas of the ten directions and three times,
together with their disciples— I now offer worship and praise with a single-minded heart.
With offerings of flower scents, lamps, incense, and perfumed water, And with exquisite food, music, and dance—
these actual offerings as they appear to the mind— I pray that all the noble ones will joyfully accept them. From beginningless time until now,
whatever ten non-virtuous actions And five acts of immediate retribution I have committed, [I confess them all].
I confess all evil deeds committed due to the afflictions of the mind.
I rejoice without exception in all the merit and virtue accumulated throughout the three periods of time by śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and even all ordinary sentient beings.
In accordance with all the aspirations of sentient beings, may you employ your various and distinct wisdoms to suit their capacities—
whether great or small, ordinary or noble— and exhort them to turn the sublime wheel of Dharma.
From this day forth until the end of saṃsāra, we pray that you remain forever in the world and do not pass into parinirvāṇa.
For the sake of all sentient beings within the ocean of suffering, may the Holy Mother regard me with her compassionate eye.
May all the merit and virtue I have now gathered become the cause for unsurpassed enlightenment.
I pray that before long, for the sake of all beings, you may realize the state of the Unsurpassed Guide.
Venerable Mother of Buddhas, endowed with great compassion,
May you swiftly purify all obscurations for me and for all sentient beings, and fulfill our accumulations of merit and wisdom.
May we attain the realization of enlightenment until reaching the state of unsurpassed bodhi, And may we always obtain peace and happiness in every lifetime.
In all places where one cultivates enlightenment, may all interruptions— whether from māras,
malevolent spirits, diseases, or the various classes of celestial beings and long-lived deities—
as well as all evil dreams, inauspicious signs, the eight fears, and all harmful afflictions, be swiftly and completely eliminated.
May all mundane and supramundane things— every source of virtue, joy, abundance, prosperity,
and every beneficial matter— be spontaneously accomplished;
may the flourishing of the Dharma through diligent practice increase, and may you always behold the countenance of the Sage.
May the intention for awakening that realizes the meaning of emptiness increase momentarily like the crescent moon,
and may the assemblies of those Buddhas all become pure. At that time,
I shall be born from a supreme lotus and behold the Tathāgata Amitābha face-to-face, receiving the prophecy of my own awakening.

I pray that you, the Mother of all the Buddhas’ deeds throughout the three times—dwelling in this world, with one face, two arms, and a green body, holding an *utpala* flower, the subtle essence of the Auspicious Buddha-Mother (Śrī-Bhagavatī)—together with your retinue, may your lifespan be long. How [is it]? May it be so.
What are their realms and what are their names? May we all likewise be so.
We praise and extol the power of your subtle virtue, O Venerable One;
Wherever we may dwell in any direction, may disease, poverty, and strife be entirely eliminated, And may you grant that all auspiciousness and excellence increase.
I pay homage to the Mother of the World-Honored One.
By the merit I have accumulated, may all sentient beings in the world-systems be born in the Land of Ultimate Bliss;
may they cast off physical faults to acquire the marks and signs of excellence, and cast off verbal faults to obtain the voice of a kalaviṅka bird.
Having abandoned mental faults and realized all-knowledge, she has attained supreme, auspicious, and meritorious signs.
This concludes the *Twenty-One Homages to the Noble Tārā, the Buddha-Mother Who Saves*.
